title: Bent lantern: a burst across a boundary
explanation: Both layouts send the same 16 payload bits in 28 channel bits, and both flip exactly channel positions 6 through 9. Consecutive order puts positions 6 and 7 into row 1 at block positions 6 and 7; channel positions 8 and 9 hit row 2 at block positions 1 and 2. Each of these rows has two errors. The syndrome decoder attempts flips at block positions 1 and 3 respectively, leaving recovered rows 1010 and 1100 instead of 1001 and 0100. In depth-four interleaved order, channel positions 6, 7, 8 and 9 hit row 2 position 2, row 3 position 2, row 4 position 2 and row 1 position 3. Each block therefore has exactly one error, which this Hamming(7,4) decoder corrects. Ordering spreads the burst without adding bits. This case demonstrates a four-bit burst, not guaranteed recovery for larger bursts. The error counts and original-picture comparison use simulator knowledge; a syndrome alone does not certify recovery.

verification.method: Decode immutable receipt artifacts to a temporary directory, verify SHA256, then call model.run(picture, burst_start - 1, burst_length, layout) for both layouts and model.outcome. Compare stored errors, decoded rows, syndromes, changed count and match verdict with those outputs. Independently inspect the channel-to-block positions described above.
verification.limits: Model evaluation only. No browser play, native keyboard, layout or learning-quality witness. The challenge author knows this solution and cannot supply the later unspoiled prediction.
